title: What did you do yesterday?
goal: Talk about things that have happened, using Romanian's everyday past tense: the *perfect compus* — the helper *am, ai, a…* plus a participle that never changes.
bekal: tell what you did yesterday, last week, or last year
form participles from all four verb groups: *lucrat, vorbit, văzut, făcut, mers*
use *a fost* to rate an experience and *am fost la…* to say you've been somewhere

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Ce ai făcut ieri?
dialogs.intro: Evening at the apartment. Andrei has just come back from Cluj and has hardly seen Budi all week, so there's a lot to ask.

lines.speaker: Andrei:
lines.text: Salut, Budi! Ce ai făcut ieri? Nu ai fost acasă.
lines.id: Hi, Budi! What did you do yesterday? You weren't home.
lines.literal: greeting, Budi! what you-have made yesterday? not you-have been at-home.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Am lucrat toată ziua. Am avut o zi lungă la birou.
lines.id: I worked all day. I had a long day at the office.
lines.literal: I-have worked all-f day-the. I-have had a-f day long-f at office.

lines.speaker: Andrei:
lines.id: And in the evening? You came home late.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Seara am mâncat la restaurant cu Ioana. Am mâncat sarmale cu mămăligă.
lines.id: In the evening I ate at a restaurant with Ioana. We had sarmale with mămăligă.
lines.literal: evening-the I/we-have eaten at restaurant with Ioana. we-have eaten sarmale with mămăligă.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Foarte bune! Și tu, ce ai făcut?
lines.id: Really good! And you, what did you do?
lines.literal: very good-f-pl! and you, what you-have made?

lines.speaker: Andrei:
lines.text: Am stat acasă și am învățat pentru examen. Apoi a fost un film românesc la televizor. Ai văzut filmul?
lines.id: I stayed home and studied for my exam. Then there was a Romanian movie on TV. Did you see the movie?
lines.literal: I-have stayed at-home and I-have studied for exam. then it-has been a-m movie romanian on television. you-have seen movie-the?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Nu, n-am văzut filmul. Am ajuns acasă la unsprezece.
lines.id: No, I didn't see the movie. I got home at eleven.
lines.literal: no, not-I-have seen movie-the. I-have arrived at-home at eleven.

lines.speaker: Andrei:
lines.text: Păcat! Apropo, unde ai fost săptămâna trecută?
lines.id: Too bad! By the way, where were you last week?
lines.literal: pity! by-the-way, where you-have been week-the past-f?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Săptămâna trecută am fost la Sibiu, cu colegii.
lines.id: Last week I went to Sibiu with my coworkers.
lines.literal: week-the past-f I-have been at Sibiu, with colleague-pl-the.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: A fost foarte frumos. Am mers mult pe jos și am făcut multe fotografii.
lines.id: It was really beautiful. We walked a lot and I took lots of photos.
lines.literal: it-has been very beautiful. we-have gone much on foot and I-have made many-f-pl photo-pl.

lines.speaker: Andrei:
lines.text: Sibiul este un oraș minunat. Eu am fost acolo acum doi ani.
lines.id: Sibiu is a wonderful city. I was there two years ago.
lines.literal: Sibiu-the it-is a-m city wonderful. I I-have been there now two-m year-pl.

notes: **Am lucrat — two words for one tense.** The Romanian past is made from a helper (*am*) and a participle (*lucrat*) — just like English "I have worked". The difference: Romanian uses this one form for "I worked yesterday", "I have worked", and "I did work" alike — spoken Romanian doesn't distinguish them.

**Am mâncat: I or we?** The helper for *eu* and *noi* is the same, *am*. In the dialogue, *am mâncat la restaurant cu Ioana* can mean "I ate" or "we ate" — context decides. If you need to be clear, add the pronoun, as Andrei does in the last line: ***Eu** am fost acolo*.

**N-am văzut filmul.** *Nu* + *am* merge into *n-am* in speech; the full *nu am* is just as correct and sounds a little more emphatic. A Romanian would actually answer even more briefly, *Nu, nu l-am văzut* ("no, I didn't see it") — pronouns in the past tense come in unit 15; for now just repeat the noun.

**Am fost la Sibiu = I went to Sibiu.** Literally "I have been to Sibiu", like the English. For a finished trip — gone and back — Romanians almost always use *am fost*, not *am mers*. *Am mers* stresses the way of going: *am mers mult pe jos*, "we walked a lot".

**Acum doi ani.** *Acum* alone means "now", but *acum* + a length of time means "… ago": *acum două zile* (two days ago), *acum o oră* (an hour ago). Note *săptămâna trecută* too: *trecută* is the participle of *a trece* (pass) used as an adjective — "the week that has passed", just like English "past".

grammars.title: Perfect compus — *am, ai, a, am, ați, au* + participle
body: The helper is a short version of *a avea*. You know three of the six forms already; **the three that differ** need special attention: third person singular ***a*** (not *are*), and *noi* ***am***, *voi* ***ați*** (not *avem, aveți*).
The participle **never changes** — not for the subject, not for gender, not for number. Learn *lucrat* once and all six forms are ready.
after: **Negative:** *nu* goes before the helper, and in speech the two merge: *n-am, n-ai, n-a, n-am, n-ați, n-au*. *N-am lucrat ieri. N-ați văzut filmul? Andrei n-a venit.*

**The helper and participle are almost inseparable.** Time and place words go before or after the pair, not in the middle: *Ieri am lucrat mult* or *Am lucrat mult ieri* — not *am ieri lucrat*. For a question, just raise your voice: *Ai mâncat?*

**Adjectives still agree, even though the participle stays put.** *Filmul a fost bun. Sarmalele au fost bune.* What changes is the helper (*a → au*) and the adjective (*bun → bune*); *fost* stays *fost*.

Romanian has other past tenses (the *imperfect*, touched on in unit 20; the *perfect simplu*, alive in novels and in the Oltenia region). For everyday conversation, the *perfect compus* covers almost everything.

grammars.title: Forming the participle
body: The participle is built from the infinitive, and its ending depends on the verb group summarized in unit 8. Three groups are completely regular; only the *-e* group splits in two and has to be learned verb by verb.

head: Infinitive
Participle
Example
Note
rows: *a lucra → lucrat*, *a mânca → mâncat*, *a învăța → învățat*, *a sta → stat*
*a vorbi → vorbit*, *a dormi → dormit*, *a veni → venit*, *a citi → citit*
*a vedea → văzut*, *a avea → avut*, *a putea → putut*, *a vrea → vrut*
*a face → făcut*, *a începe → început*, *a trece → trecut*, *a cere → cerut*
*a merge → mers*, *a scrie → scris*, *a pune → pus*, *a zice → zis*, *a ajunge → ajuns*
the *-e* and the last consonant drop
*a fi → fost*, *a ști → știut*, *a bea → băut*

after: **Branch *-ut* or *-s*?** There's no fully reliable rule; dictionaries always list it. A rough guide: verbs whose *eu* form ends in *-g, -d, -n* lean toward *-s* (*merg → mers, ajung → ajuns, deschid → deschis, pun → pus, spun → spus*). The full list of participles used in this book is in unit 15.

**The participle also works as an adjective** — and then it agrees like a four-form adjective: *săptămâna trecută*, *anul trecut*, *ușa este deschisă*, *magazinele sunt închise*. Many adjectives you already know are participles in disguise: *obosit* (tired), *ocupat* (busy), *căsătorit* (married).

blocks.text: *Trecut* agrees with its noun: *săptămâna trecut**ă***, *luna trecut**ă*** (f), but *anul trecut*, *weekendul trecut* (m/n). Day names for a one-off event are used **without** the article — *luni am lucrat* ("on Monday I worked") — unlike *lunea* with the article from unit 7, which means "every Monday". And *încă nu* goes before the helper: *Încă n-am mâncat* = "I haven't eaten yet".

blocks.title: Story glue: four words that make your story flow
items: ***Mai întâi*** (first): *Mai întâi am băut o cafea.*
***Apoi*** or ***după aceea*** (then, after that): *Apoi am mers la birou cu metroul.*
***La prânz… seara…*** — the parts of the day from unit 7 still work as signposts: *La prânz am mâncat o ciorbă. Seara am citit puțin.*
***La sfârșit*** (in the end): *La sfârșit am dormit zece ore!* With these four links and ten participles, you can already tell the story of a whole day.

sections.title: *A fost* — rating things, and places you've been

head: Sentence
English
rows: It was really beautiful. / It was great.
It went well. · It was hard.
Was it expensive? — No, it wasn't expensive.
*Unde ai fost ieri?* — *Am fost la piață.*
Where were you yesterday? — I went to the market.
*Ați fost la Brașov?* — *Da, am fost anul trecut.*
Have you been to Brașov? — Yes, last year.
*A fost un concert în Centrul Vechi.*
There was a concert in the Old Town.

blocks.text: In the past tense *a fi* works like any other verb: *am fost, ai fost, a fost, am fost, ați fost, au fost*. Keep its three jobs apart. **Rating**: *a fost* + an adjective in the masculine singular when you rate the situation in general (*a fost frumos*), and agreeing when the thing is named (*excursia a fost frumoasă*). **There was**: *a fost un film la televizor* — "there was a movie". **Been to**: *am fost la* + place, the most natural way to say "I went to…" or "I've been to…".

blocks.title: Sibiu, the city whose houses have eyes
items: Sibiu lies in Transylvania, about five hours by train from Bucharest. Its old town was built by German Saxon settlers in the Middle Ages, and its German name, *Hermannstadt*, still appears on city signs.
Its trademark is the eyelid-shaped attic windows on the old roofs — people call them *ochii Sibiului*, "the eyes of Sibiu". Note the genitive: *Sibiul → Sibiului*, exactly the pattern from unit 13.

Two places that turn up in everyone's photos: *Piața Mare* (the Great Square) and *Podul Minciunilor*, "the Bridge of Lies" — *minciunilor* is the genitive plural of *minciuni* (lies). In 2007 Sibiu was a European Capital of Culture.
Every Romanian fairy tale opens with the same past tense as this unit: ***A fost odată ca niciodată…*** — "Once upon a time, like never before…".
